notes: Use-case summary: live agent assist across voice and web chat. Real-time streaming suggestions (token-by-token), dynamic tool-calling to CRM and ticketing system, on-the-fly ticket summarization at call wrap-up.
SLOs: end-to-end suggestion latency target  <= 150ms median, P95 <= 300ms. For voice disfluency handling want suggestion latency under 200ms perceived by agent.
Throughput profile: typical 150-250 concurrent agents, burst to 1,500+ during promo spikes (need graceful degradation). Cost sensitivity: care about per-token cost during bursts.

Model preferences: prefer open quantized models for private deployment; want fallback chain: red-ops high-quality (p98), then faster quantized variant for spikes. Function calling required for CRM create/update.
Security: must support customer-managed keys (KMS), SSO/SAML for agent desktop, audit logs with 90-day retention, optional EU residency for specific customers.
Guardrails requested: hallucination filters for legal/financial intents, deterministic ticket-summary mode for compliance, configurable blocklist and entity redaction rules.
POC ask: 2-week sim with 200 concurrent agents, live voice + chat integration, measure streaming latency, token cost under defined workload, validate tool-calling reliability and idempotence.
Quote: VP of Product - 'If suggestions are slower than 250ms agents will ignore them; we need near-instant relevance.'
Logs / artifacts: provided sample call transcripts and agent flows in Drive (/drive/security), Fireflies transcripts linked above.
Redwood suggested: Dedicated with autoscale bursts, prefix/KV caching, quantization recommendations from Optimize, and fallback routing by latency tier.
POC success metrics: median suggestion latency <=160ms, P95 <=300ms, tool-calling success rate >=99.5%, token cost reduction >=25% vs baseline using caching/batching
